questions_and_answers.question_text: What is the negative of the verb shì, and what does it mean?
Which syllable is the equivalent of English "not"?
Which tone does bù take before a syllable in the High, Rising, or Low tone?
Why is bú used in the phrase bú shi, even though shi is pronounced in the Neutral tone?
Give the four example phrases with fēi/féi/fěi/fèi and their English meanings.
What determines the tone of the syllable bù?

answers.answer_text: The tone of the syllable which follows it.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which tone does bù take before a syllable in the Falling or Neutral tone?

answers.answer_text: A Rising tone is used — bú.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which form of the syllable is the basic form, and when is it used?

answers.answer_text: Bù is the basic form. It is used when the syllable stands alone as a short "no" answer, and when it is discussed.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Why do almost all of the first few verbs learned take bú?

answers.answer_text: Because almost all of them happen to be in the Falling tone, and bù becomes bú before a Falling tone.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese sentence meaning "I'm not Mr. Mǎ."

articles.text:
4. A: Nǐ shi Mǎ Xiānsheng ma?               Are you Mr. Mǎ?
   B: Wǒ bú shi Mǎ Xiānsheng.               I'm not Mr. Mǎ.

5. A: Wǒ shi Wáng Dànián.                   I am Wáng Dànián.
   B: Wǒ bú shi Wáng Dànián.                I'm not Wáng Dànián.

Notes on Nos. 4-5

The negative of the verb shì, "to be," is bù shì, "not to be." The equivalent of "not" is the syllable bù. The tone for the syllable bù depends on the tone of the following syllable. When followed by a syllable with a High, Rising, or Low tone, a Falling tone is used (bù). When followed by a syllable with a Falling or Neutral tone, a Rising tone is used (bú).

bù fēi   (not to fly)
bù féi   (not to be fat)
bù fěi   (not to slander)
bú fèi   (not to waste)

Almost all of the first few verbs you learn happen to be in the Falling tone, and so take bú. But remember that bù is the basic form. That is the form the syllable takes when it stands alone as a short "no" answer--Bù--and when it is discussed, as in "Bù means 'not'."

Notice that even though shì, "to be," is usually pronounced in the Neutral tone in the phrase bú shi, the original Falling tone of shì still causes bù to be pronounced with a Rising tone: bú.
